parsedVerdict.reasoning: This module fails the rule because its two files reach persistence in different ways. BoxOffice.ts only touches persistence through the module's store ports: EventStore (load, saveSeatsSold, upcoming) and TicketStore (load, add, markScanned). GateLog.ts skips that layer. It takes PrismaService directly and calls the ORM itself: prisma.scan.create in scanned() and prisma.scan.findMany in busiestGate(). I checked both candidate flags against the source and both are confirmed. Because of this, the module has no single persistence boundary. GateLog also puts a raw Prisma query and in-memory aggregation inside a domain class, while BoxOffice works through domain types. A smaller point: BoxOffice.ts builds an Event from a stored row the same way twice, in purchase() and in listing(), instead of calling one shared mapper. That is minor repetition of mapping code, not a duplicated business rule.

violations.message: GateLog calls the Prisma ORM directly (PrismaService: scan.create, scan.findMany) and skips the store/repository ports that the rest of the module uses (EventStore, TicketStore), so the module has no single persistence boundary.
